target_customer: Job seekers, especially students and new graduates, with a free browser extension, plus paid premium features and recruiters
problem: Applying to many jobs means retyping the same details on each company's form. Simplify Copilot autofills applications and tracks them.
business_model: Freemium job seeker tools with premium subscription and recruiter services; still experimenting with monetization in Feb 2024

founders.name: Michael Yan
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the co-founders conceived the idea in college while applying to hundreds of jobs.

competitors.name: Teal
competitors.what: Job application tracker and career tools with a Job Tracker product
competitors.traction_then: Job Tracker launched on Product Hunt in Nov 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension that autofills many different applicant tracking system forms is brittle and needs constant maintenance, but is standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Autofill is copyable, but a large student user base and the SimplifyJobs internship lists on GitHub (maintained with Pitt CSC) create distribution that rivals lacked.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2024) contrasts Simplify with LinkedIn but names no copying; many autofill and AI apply tools arrived by 2026 per comparison pages.

market_need_then: Founders felt the pain applying to hundreds of jobs in college (TechCrunch 2024). Simplify's Product Hunt launch was October 2021 per a launch tracker.

branding.domain_note: Uses simplify.jobs on a .jobs domain; the name is shared with many unrelated firms, so searches mix results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission led: 'Helping a billion people build their dream career' (YC page)

branding.brand_signature: SimplifyJobs GitHub internship lists maintained with the Pitt Computer Science Club
branding.community_and_virality: SimplifyJobs repositories list over 1,700 internship roles for Summer 2026 and are a major discovery channel among students per the repository README.

brand_strength.rationale: The GitHub internship lists are a well known student asset that drive awareness, but the name is generic and confusable with other Simplify brands.

outcome_analysis: Simplify reached over 1M users per the YC page with a small team and very little capital, using free tools and community maintained internship lists for distribution. It raised a $3M seed only in February 2024 with about 10 employees. Competition from AI apply tools increased, so the company remains a capital efficient consumer product with an unproven monetization.
notes: The YC page links a Forbes headline from June 2022 reporting a $1.2M raise; Forbes was not opened and only one source appears, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. CB Insights lists a 2022 round at $20M that looks like a valuation, and total raised varies from $3.2M to $4.3M across aggregators. TechCrunch names only Michael Yan; the YC page names three founders. YC page team size conflicts (5 vs 7). Huntr was considered but only a January 2022 Product Hunt launch was found, so it is not listed.
